voice.persona: Two fixed companion voices (companions.md §5): Dr. Omar, lead host — male, late 30s, friendly, confident, medium-low pitch; Noor, co-host — female, early-to-mid 30s, warm, calm, clear. Neither voice may be cloned from or resemble a real employee. Provider and voice ids pending program D10.

segments.narration: NOOR: Welcome to Safety in Practice: Hazard, Fire & Chemical Lab. You will practise decisions that help you act with confidence. You will leave with practical actions for your next shift.
segments.on_screen_text: "Safety in Practice" · "Hazard, fire and chemical lab"
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Safety is the habits that protect life, health and environment. Today you practise them.
segments.on_screen_text: "Safety = measures that protect life, health and environment." · "Today you practise, not read."
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Walk through the wet-floor example aloud.
segments.on_screen_text: Problem: wet floor at the clinic entrance during rain. Steps: (1) name the hazard; (2) likelihood 4 (busy entrance) ; (3) impact 3 (fall injury); (4) risk = 4 × 3 = 12; (5) control: mat + sign + mop …
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: There are six hazards. I walked past a blocked exit for a week before I noticed it.
segments.on_screen_text: New illustration of a store room/office (based on p.4 idea). Answer key (6 regions): trailing cables across the walkway · boxes stacked above shoulder height · blocked fire exit / extinguisher · unlabelled bottle on a shelf · liquid spill …
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Decide as you would on shift, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: "Which hazard in the room do you report and fix first?" → blocked fire exit (high impact for everyone)
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Write the note as you would in the record, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: "Likelihood 2, impact 5. Risk score = ___" → accepted: 10
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: The poster on the wall is bilingual. Learn both names. Check your site's extensions.
segments.on_screen_text: 10 colour codes + 2 announcements; front EN + AR name and colour chip, back meaning + extension (D2). Code Blue 2222
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: There is no timer, but in real life seconds matter. Play the round, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: Setting: afternoon clinic, smoke from a consultation room. Nodes: (1) Rescue — patient in the room vs. phone first; (2) Alarm — shout "Code Red", pull the call point, then choose the complete call script (code type + location + …
segments.speaker: noor

segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: NOOR: Place each item where it belongs, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: Items: "Bedbound adult on the 2nd floor", "Adult who can't walk, stairs needed", "Newborn in the nursery", "Infant carried by staff" → targets: Evacuation mattress · Evacuation chair · Newborn evacuation chair · Baby mover / apron
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Label the parts you can name, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: Generic own floor plan (Zones A–E). Place 6 labels: call point · extinguisher · fire hose reel · fire blanket · evacuation route · assembly point ("you are here" given)
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Inside vs outside assembly points. Find your unit's plan today.
segments.on_screen_text: Inside assembly point · Outside assembly point · "Find your unit's plan on the wall today." Horizontal → vertical → full (recap from 01)
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Before you need it, know how to read the label and check the gauge.
segments.on_screen_text: Own photo of a My Clinic dry-powder extinguisher. Regions: safety pin · pressure gauge (needle in green) · class / agent label · instructions panel (PASS) · last inspection tag
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Place each item where it belongs, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: Scenes: "Sparking computer", "Pan of oil in the staff kitchen", "Burning cardboard", "Spilled solvent on fire" → CO₂ · Wet chemical · Water / ABC powder · Foam
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: HAZMAT is chemical or biological. One clear rule decides Code Orange.
segments.on_screen_text: Definition (p.21) · Code Orange = chemical or biological release · Rule from D1
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Two kits, two colours, two jobs.
segments.on_screen_text: Before = Chemical spill kit (red case) · After = Biological spill kit (yellow, biohazard) · caption: contents of each
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Play the situation through and decide, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: 3 nodes: (1) urine sample dropped in the lab corridor → biological kit, no Code Orange; (2) large spill of surface disinfectant above the threshold → Code Orange; (3) small amount of a reagent marked "highly toxic" → Code Orange …
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Put the steps in the order you would follow at work, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: 7 steps (B4): PPE per SDS → isolate & warn → contain the edges → absorb / neutralise → bag, seal, label → clean & report → restock the kit
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Read a register row left to right: what it is, why it's here, is the SDS on file, what the diamond says.
segments.on_screen_text: Anonymised register table (5 rows, from B5): name · hazard class · purpose · quantity · SDS ✓ · NFPA H/F/R/S. Callouts on the SDS and NFPA columns
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Match each item to the person or step that owns it, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: 9 pairs: pictogram ↔ example hazard text from p.23 (e.g. Flame over circle ↔ "oxidiser — can intensify fire")
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Decide as you would on shift, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: Row: "Surface disinfectant X — SDS ✘". "You need it for a cleaning task now. What do you do?" → don't use; report the missing SDS to your supervisor / EHS
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Decide as you would on shift, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: Row shows NFPA 2-3-0. "Where must it be stored?" → approved flammable cabinet, away from heat
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: The store is locked. Four checks open it. Everything you need is in this module. Work through each step in turn, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: Intro: the store door is locked; four checks unlock it. Puzzles: (1) "Health rating of the solvent on the diamond?" → 2; (2) "Which register row is missing its SDS? Enter the row number." → 4; (3) "How many minutes …
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Place each item where it belongs, then read the feedback.
segments.on_screen_text: Items: scented candle · personal fan heater · extension cord from home · e-cigarette · Facilities-approved power strip · BME-tagged suction unit · reheating lunch for 10 minutes · kettle in the staff pantry (approved) → Allowed / Prohibited (union …
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: Your results are organised by objective. Notice where you were confident, then revisit any section that needs another practical try. Use that insight to choose what to revisit.
segments.on_screen_text: hs2-o1…o7, weak below 70%
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: This reflection is not scored. Choose the response that helps you set one intention for your next shift.
segments.on_screen_text: "Name one hazard you'll check in your own area this week."
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: NOOR: You can now use these key actions in your role. Keep the practical rule close, ask when you are unsure, and carry the next step into your shift. Take one clear next action with you.
